chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Shu'ayb who linked it up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The most pious person is one who stops when in doubt. The best worshipping person is one who performs the obligatory deeds. The most ascetic person is one who abandons the forbidden, and the most hard-working person is one who abandons sinning.
ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics of the most pious, worshipped, ascetic, and hard-working people according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this concise definition from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that reorients traditional spiritual concepts toward practical ethical boundaries: piety (*wara'*) is defined by caution in doubtful matters, while true asceticism (*zuhd*) is identified with the avoidance of the forbidden (*haram*). This framework emphasizes that spiritual excellence is not merely about ritual volume but about the precision of one's adherence to divine limits, a key theme in Shia ethical jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-56 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Abi Shoayb who linked it up to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) who said, “

The most pious person is one who stops when in doubt. The best worshipping person is one who performs the obligatory deeds. The most ascetic person is one who abandons the forbidden, and the most hard-working person is one who abandons sinning.”
